questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless genital ulcer with indurated edges and a clean base. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged, rubbery, and non-tender. Dark-field microscopy shows corkscrew-motile organisms. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: This is primary syphilis caused by Treponema pallidum. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose is the first-line treatment for primary and secondary syphilis per WHO and IADVL guidelines.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a 3-month history of hypopigmented anesthetic patches on the trunk. Skin smear from the lesion shows 1-2 AFB per 100 oil-immersion fields (BI = 1+). Histopathology shows epithelioid cell granulomas with a grenz zone. What is the Ridley-Jopling classification of this patient?
questions.exp: Borderline tuberculoid (BT) leprosy shows epithelioid granulomas with a grenz zone, and skin smears may show scanty AFB (BI 1-2+). TT would be smear-negative; BB and BL would have higher BI and less well-formed granulomas.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman develops tense bullae on normal-appearing skin and erythematous plaques, predominantly on the flexures and trunk. Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone. Which autoantigen is primarily targeted?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid is characterized by IgG autoantibodies against BP180 (BPAG2, type XVII collagen) and BP230 (BPAG1). Linear IgG/C3 at BMZ on DIF is the hallmark. Desmoglein 3 is targeted in pemphigus vulgaris.

questions.q: A 22-year-old HIV-positive man (CD4 count 80 cells/μL) presents with multiple painless, umbilicated, flesh-colored papules on the face and genitals. The causative virus belongs to which family?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by Molluscum contagiosum virus (MCV), a large DNA virus belonging to the Poxviridae family. It is particularly widespread in immunocompromised individuals.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with butterfly-shaped erythema on the face, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA is positive (1:640, homogeneous pattern). Anti-dsDNA antibodies are strongly positive. Which complement component level is most characteristically reduced in active disease?
questions.exp: In active SLE, complement consumption through the classical pathway leads to low serum C3 and C4 levels. C3 is the central complement component and its reduction is the most reliable marker of disease activity and immune complex deposition.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man on long-term hydroxyurea for polycythemia vera develops painful leg ulcers over the medial malleoli and hyperpigmented macules on the lower limbs. Which mechanism best explains the hydroxyurea-induced leg ulcers?
opts: Impaired DNA repair leading to dermal fibrosis and vascular insufficiency
Fixed drug eruption at pressure sites
questions.exp: Hydroxyurea causes leg ulcers (most commonly over medial malleoli) through impaired DNA repair in endothelial cells, reduced angiogenesis, and local vascular damage. These ulcers are notoriously slow to heal and often require drug discontinuation.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent papule with telangiectasias on the nose, present for 2 years. Dermoscopy reveals arborizing vessels and shiny white structureless areas. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Nodular basal cell carcinoma (BCC) classically appears as a pearly papule with rolled edges and arborizing telangiectasias on sun-exposed skin. Dermoscopy shows arborizing vessels and shiny white structures (chrysalis structures). It is the most common skin malignancy.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with intense pruritus and erythematous papulovesicles on the extensor surfaces of elbows, knees, and buttocks. She also has a history of gluten-sensitive enteropathy. Direct immunofluorescence shows granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillae tips. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) is characterized by granular IgA at dermal papillae tips and is associated with celiac disease. First-line treatment is dapsone (for rapid symptom control) combined with a strict gluten-free diet (for long-term remission).

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman from Rajasthan presents with a chronic painless ulcer on the forearm with a 'volcano crater' appearance and painless lymphadenopathy. Slit-skin smear shows oval bodies inside macrophages. What is the vector responsible for transmitting this disease?
questions.exp: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (Oriental sore) is caused by Leishmania tropica, transmitted by the female Phlebotomus sandfly. Amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) are seen inside macrophages on smear.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery-white scales on the scalp, elbows, and knees for 5 years. Nail examination reveals pitting, onycholysis, and oil spots. Auspitz sign is positive. Which cytokine pathway is central to the pathogenesis of plaque psoriasis?
questions.exp: Plaque psoriasis pathogenesis is driven primarily by the IL-23/Th17 axis. IL-23 (from dendritic cells) drives Th17 cell differentiation producing IL-17A, IL-17F, and IL-22, which stimulate keratinocyte proliferation and neutrophil recruitment. This is the target of secukinumab, ixekizumab (anti-IL-17) and guselkumab, risankizumab (anti-IL-23) biologics.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth following an upper respiratory tract infection. Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. Which organism is the most common causative agent today?
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus, which appears as gram-positive cocci in clusters. It presents with honey-colored crusted lesions. S. pyogenes can also cause impetigo but S. aureus is now the predominant organism.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate develops painful vesicles along the T5 dermatome on the right side. Which antiviral combination is most effective in reducing post-herpetic neuralgia when started within 72 hours of rash onset?
opts: Both valacyclovir and famciclovir are superior to acyclovir for reducing PHN
questions.exp: Valacyclovir (1g TID) and famciclovir (500mg TID) for 7 days have been shown to be superior to acyclovir in reducing the duration and severity of post-herpetic neuralgia due to higher bioavailability and sustained plasma levels compared to acyclovir.

questions.q: A 28-year-old primigravida at 32 weeks gestation develops intensely pruritic urticarial papules and plaques in the abdominal striae, sparing the umbilicus. DIF of perilesional skin is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy (PUPPP/pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy) characteristically starts in the abdominal striae, spares the umbilicus, DIF is negative, and is most common in primigravidae. Pemphigoid gestationis would show linear C3/IgG on DIF and typically involves the umbilicus.

questions.q: A 36-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, telangiectasias on the face and hands, and dysphagia. Anti-centromere antibody (ACA) is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: The CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) represents limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis. Anti-centromere antibody is the hallmark serological marker, found in 70-80% of CREST patients.

questions.q: A 19-year-old man presents with multiple verrucous, cauliflower-like lesions on his penis. Biopsy shows koilocytes, acanthosis, and hyperkeratosis. HPV typing shows HPV 6. What is the risk of malignant transformation with this HPV type?
opts: High risk — commonly transforms to penile carcinoma
Low risk — HPV 6 is a low-risk type
Intermediate risk — depends on immune status
Certain transformation occurs within 5 years without treatment
questions.exp: HPV 6 and HPV 11 are low-risk HPV types responsible for condyloma acuminata (genital warts). They rarely cause malignant transformation. High-risk types include HPV 16, 18, 31, 33, which are associated with squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic man presents with a rapidly spreading, foul-smelling necrotic infection of the scrotum and perineum with subcutaneous emphysema on X-ray. What is the specific term for this life-threatening condition?
questions.exp: Fournier's gangrene is a type of necrotizing fasciitis specifically affecting the perineum and genitalia. It is polymicrobial (aerobic + anaerobic bacteria) and classically occurs in diabetic men. Subcutaneous gas on imaging is pathognomonic. Requires urgent surgical debridement and broad-spectrum antibiotics.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with depigmented macules on the face and trunk since birth. Wood's lamp examination shows ivory-white fluorescence. Histopathology reveals absent melanocytes. There is a white forelock. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Piebaldism is a congenital disorder (autosomal dominant, KIT gene mutation) with absent melanocytes in affected areas. It presents at birth with white forelock and depigmented patches, often with islands of normal or hyperpigmented skin within white patches. Unlike vitiligo, melanocytes are congenitally absent, not autoimmunely destroyed.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with a 2-cm red nodule on the lower leg that bleeds easily on minor trauma, present for 6 months. Dermoscopy shows a white structureless area centrally surrounded by a red collarette. Histopathology shows lobular proliferation of blood vessels. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary hemangioma) is a benign vascular proliferation presenting as a rapidly growing, easily bleeding red nodule. Dermoscopy shows a white rail sign and red collarette. Histopathology reveals lobular arrangement of capillaries.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with scaly, hypopigmented macules on the upper trunk with fine scale on stretching (Besnier's sign). KOH mount shows short hyphae and spherical spores ('spaghetti and meatballs'). What is the most appropriate topical treatment?
opts: Topical selenium sulfide 2.5% or ketoconazole 2% shampoo
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor caused by Malassezia furfur shows characteristic 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern on KOH. First-line topical treatment includes selenium sulfide 2.5% lotion or ketoconazole 2% shampoo applied to affected areas. For extensive disease, oral itraconazole or fluconazole is used.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man on antihypertensive therapy develops a widespread blistering eruption with erosions involving mucous membranes. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposition in the epidermis (fishnet pattern). Which drug class is most commonly implicated in drug-induced pemphigus?
questions.exp: Drug-induced pemphigus most commonly occurs with thiol-containing drugs such as D-penicillamine and captopril. The DIF pattern with intercellular IgG (fishnet/chicken wire) is identical to true pemphigus vulgaris. D-penicillamine is the single most common drug implicated.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive man presents with painful perianal ulcers for 4 weeks. HSV PCR from the ulcer swab is positive. CD4 count is 50 cells/μL. What is the significance of HSV ulcers persisting beyond 1 month in an HIV-infected individual?
opts: Increased risk of secondary bacterial superinfection only
Development of HSV encephalitis is imminent
Risk of perinatal transmission if partner is pregnant
questions.exp: Chronic mucocutaneous HSV ulcers persisting for more than 1 month in an HIV-infected individual is an AIDS-defining illness (CDC Category C). Acyclovir or valacyclovir treatment is indicated; if acyclovir-resistant, foscarnet is the alternative.

questions.q: A 42-year-old leprosy patient on multi-drug therapy develops sudden appearance of new shiny erythematous tender nodules on the face and extremities with fever and arthralgias. Existing patches remain unchanged. What type of reaction is this and what is the first-line treatment?
opts: Type 1 lepra reaction — treated with corticosteroids
Type 2 lepra reaction (ENL) — treated with thalidomide or corticosteroids
Downgrading reaction — treated by adding rifampicin
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) is a Type 2 lepra reaction occurring in BL/LL leprosy, characterized by tender erythematous nodules, fever, and systemic symptoms. It is immune complex-mediated. Thalidomide is first-line for males; prednisolone is used for women of childbearing age. MDT is continued.

questions.q: A 24-year-old woman with atopic dermatitis develops widespread monomorphic umbilicated vesicles over her entire body following a cold sore contact. On examination, vesicles appear on a background of eczematous skin. What is this serious complication called?
questions.exp: Kaposi's varicelliform eruption (eczema herpeticum) is a serious complication of atopic dermatitis where HSV-1 disseminates widely over eczematous skin. It presents as monomorphic umbilicated vesicles becoming erosions and crusts. Requires systemic acyclovir treatment.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a large pigmented lesion on his back: irregular borders, multiple colors, diameter of 9 mm. Dermoscopy shows atypical pigment network, regression structures, and blue-white veil. What is the next best step in management?
opts: Excisional biopsy with 2 mm margins for histopathological diagnosis
Punch biopsy of the darkest area only
Shave biopsy and send for melanoma markers
questions.exp: A suspicious pigmented lesion with ABCDE criteria and dermoscopic features of melanoma requires excisional biopsy with narrow margins (1-2mm) to allow complete histological assessment including Breslow thickness and Clark level. Punch or shave biopsy can miss the deepest portion and are not recommended.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman undergoes patch testing. A reaction that appears at 48 hours but disappears by 96 hours is classified as:
questions.exp: In patch testing, a reaction that peaks at 48 hours and fades by 96 hours is characteristic of an irritant (non-allergic) reaction (decrescendo pattern). True allergic contact dermatitis reactions typically persist or increase in intensity from 48 to 96-120 hours (crescendo pattern).

questions.q: A 52-year-old chronic smoker presents with a 1.5 cm erythematous plaque with central ulceration on the lower lip. Biopsy reveals squamous cell carcinoma. Which histological feature indicates the worst prognosis?
opts: Well-differentiated squamous cells with keratin pearls
questions.exp: Perineural invasion in squamous cell carcinoma is associated with poor prognosis, higher risk of local recurrence, and regional lymph node metastasis. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes indicate a favorable immune response. Well-differentiated histology with keratin pearls indicates better differentiation.

questions.q: A 20-year-old woman with SLE has anti-Smith antibody positive, anti-dsDNA positive, low C3/C4, and thrombocytopenia. Which of the following antibodies has the HIGHEST specificity for SLE, though low sensitivity?
questions.exp: Anti-Smith (anti-Sm) antibody has the highest specificity for SLE (>99%) but low sensitivity (25-30%). Anti-dsDNA is also highly specific and correlates with disease activity. Anti-Ro/SSA is associated with neonatal lupus and Sjogren's syndrome. Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus.

questions.q: A 16-year-old boy has recurrent boils, folliculitis, and perianal abscesses since childhood. History reveals delayed separation of umbilical cord. Neutrophil count is markedly elevated (30,000/μL) during infection but neutrophils cannot reach the site of infection. NBT (nitroblue tetrazolium) test is normal. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is characterized by delayed umbilical cord separation, recurrent bacterial infections, and marked neutrophilia without pus formation. CD18 (beta-2 integrin) is absent, preventing neutrophil migration to infection sites. NBT test is normal in LAD (unlike CGD where oxidative burst is absent).

questions.q: A 38-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents for treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. Which systemic therapy has the most favorable safety profile considering his comorbidities?
questions.exp: In a diabetic hypertensive patient, conventional agents are limited: cyclosporine worsens hypertension and causes nephrotoxicity; methotrexate causes hepatotoxicity (worsened by metabolic syndrome); acitretin causes dyslipidemia. Secukinumab (anti-IL-17A) has a favorable safety profile with no clinically significant interactions with diabetes or hypertension medications.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman undergoes Mohs micrographic surgery for a 1.8 cm recurrent basal cell carcinoma on the nose. What is the key advantage of Mohs surgery over standard wide local excision?
opts: Complete margin assessment in real-time with maximal tissue conservation
Better cosmesis due to smaller routine excision margins
Simultaneous treatment of regional lymph nodes
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery allows 100% margin assessment of the excised tissue in real-time using frozen sections, compared to standard bread-loaf sectioning that samples only approximately 0.1% of margins. This results in the lowest recurrence rate while conserving maximum normal tissue, crucial for cosmetically sensitive areas.

questions.q: A 29-year-old woman with BMI 34 kg/m2 presents with brown, reticulated, velvety hyperpigmentation on her inner thighs and axillae. Fasting insulin level is markedly elevated. What is this condition and its primary clinical significance?
opts: Terra firma-forme dermatosis — cosmetic concern only
Acanthosis nigricans — cutaneous marker of insulin resistance
Confluent and reticulated papillomatosis — requires minocycline
questions.exp: Acanthosis nigricans presents as velvety, hyperpigmented plaques in body folds and is most commonly associated with insulin resistance and obesity. In young patients, it mandates screening for type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome. Malignant acanthosis nigricans associated with internal malignancy is typically more extensive and involves unusual sites.
